**[10-19 19:51 Beijing] GCL Technology Holdings (3800.HK) enters MOU to acquire ~82% of Sichuan GCL Lithium Battery Technology for ~RMB 2.5 billion**  
GCL Technology Holdings (3800.HK) signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MOU) on 19 Oct 2026 with the vendor to acquire ~81.91% equity in Sichuan GCL Lithium Battery Technology Co., Ltd. (四川GCL锂电池技术有限公司). Consideration: approximately RMB 2.5 billion (HK$2.9363 billion). Settlement: ~RMB 650 million (HK$763.425 million) in cash and ~RMB 1.85 billion (HK$2.1728 billion) via allotment of consideration shares at minimum issue price of ~HK$1.3 per share based on 30 June 2026 net asset value; expected not more than ~1.671 billion shares. Upon completion, target will become non wholly-owned subsidiary with consolidated results. Performance commitments: target's aggregate adjusted net profit for 2027–2028 not less than RMB 620 million; development of sixth-generation LFP cathode material (compacted density >2.8 g/cm³) by 31 Dec 2028. If commitments missed, vendor must compensate from consideration received. Completion subject to due diligence, valuation, shareholder approval, regulatory clearances, and no material adverse change. Transaction is connected transaction and may be notifiable under Listing Rules.  
_Filing · HKEX filing · GCL Technology Holdings (3800.HK), Sichuan GCL Lithium Battery Technology Co., Ltd. · [Source](https://www1.hkexnews.hk/listedco/listconews/sehk/2026/1019/2026101900265.pdf)_

**[10-19 19:09 Beijing] Xi'an Yisi Wafer (西安奕材, 688783.SH) Q3 2026 net profit 441m yuan, up 3x on market recovery**  
Xi'an Yisi Wafer (西安奕材, 688783.SH) reported Q3 2026 revenue 1.062bn yuan (+68.50% YoY), net profit 441m yuan (+302.55% YoY), excluding non-recurring items loss 153m yuan (vs. loss 217m yuan prior year). Nine-month revenue 2.651bn yuan (+37.16% YoY), net profit 151m yuan (swing to profitability from loss), excluding non-recurring items loss 473m yuan. Shipments ~331m wafers (Q3), up 68% YoY; cumulative 830m wafers (9M), up 42.7%. 12-inch wafer market entered supply deficit on AI-chip, HBM, and datacenter demand surge. Gross margin 6.45% (Q3), up 4.03pp YoY; nine-month margin 5.13%, up 1.11pp. Product-mix upgraded: standard wafers now 84% of sales (up 5.4pp), epitaxial wafers 30.8% (up 11.0pp). Cost absorption hindered by factory 2 depreciation still ramping; pricing gains from Q1 2026 negotiations to be realized in 2027. Domestic market share #1; top supplier to major domestic memory/logic makers; shipping to TSMC, Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron, Kioxia, GlobalFoundries, Powertech, UMC, others. Q4-Q3 guidance: cumulative 210 qualified customers (+21 in quarter), 147 qualified standard-wafer specs (+5).  
_Filing · SSE/SZSE filing · Xi'an Yisi Wafer (西安奕材, 688783.SH) · [Source](https://data.eastmoney.com/notices/detail/688783/AN202610191830689663.html)_

**[10-19 17:49 Beijing] Rayfan Technology 9M 2026 guidance: revenue 4.1-4.3 billion yuan up 36-42%; net profit 1.58-1.68 billion yuan up 70-80%**  
Rayfan Technology (赛分科技, 688758.SH) 9M 2026 guidance: revenue 4.1-4.3 billion yuan up 36-42% YoY; net profit 1.58-1.68 billion yuan up 70-80% YoY; non-GAAP net profit 1.54-1.64 billion yuan up 81-93% YoY. Company pursuing dual-track strategy in chromatographic separation materials and industrial purification; leveraging 20+ years of chromatography expertise; expanding operations with full US/China production base setup strengthening core competitiveness. 2026 as '15th Five-Year Plan' start year, biotech becoming national emerging pillar industry with favorable policy. Global blockbuster biologics entering patent cliff, biosimilar R&D accelerating, raising upstream purification material demand. Company targets antibody, insulin/peptide, GLP-1, recombinant protein, small RNA purification; focuses on late-stage clinical and commercialization projects. New projects landed in period: 28 late-stage and commercial-stage projects, serving as growth engine. Front-loaded pipeline projects now entering late-stage and commercial phases, driving customer demand and order scale expansion; existing customer re-orders stable providing base. Management focused: period expense ratio down YoY, cost control effective, profit elasticity releasing, profit growth outpacing revenue.

**[10-19 20:05 Beijing] Israeli startup DoubleAI raises $220M to reduce enterprise compute costs with new AI category**  
Tel Aviv startup DoubleAI announced it will launch a new artificial intelligence category to help enterprises reduce computing costs. The company's co-founder and CEO Amnon Shashua is also the founder of autonomous driving company Mobileye. DoubleAI's investors include Lightspeed Venture Partners, Bessemer Venture Partners, Nvidia and Dell, with total funding of $220 million. DoubleAI calls this new AI category a "Code Execution Model" (CEM), positioning it between code and chips. Large language models can help humans write code, while code execution models are embedded in running programs and work without human intervention.

## Semiconductors (14)

🔴 **[10-19 22:56 Beijing] US Defense Department's Chief Technology Officer: considering investment in microelectronics firms**  
Emil Michael, the US Department of Defense's Chief Technology Officer, said in an interview that the Pentagon is "monitoring microelectronics firms" and companies in supply chain segments currently handled only by ASML and TSMC. Michael stated the Pentagon is also "monitoring drone components, as some are currently dependent on adversary-country suppliers, such as Russian motors and batteries." He added that the Pentagon will "continuously push more deals" over the next 12 months, with focus on battery supply, critical minerals and aerospace.

Micron disclosed it is developing Edge Inference Memory (EIM) specifically designed for physical AI applications. The technology aims to reduce data processing latency and improve bandwidth, with industry sources expecting volume production in H2 2028. Nvidia has requested Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron to standardize adoption of TSMC's 3nm process for manufacturing HBM base chips to promote product standardization. Samsung reportedly plans to adopt TSMC's 3nm process for producing next-generation custom high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for Nvidia.

The round was led by newly established investment firm Trace Capital with Innovation X as co-lead, with participation from SanDisk, T. Rowe Price, Cadence's venture capital division and others. Existing shareholders including ARK Invest and Fidelity Investments continued to participate. Compared to the $2.6 billion valuation in the previous round in 2024, Tenstorrent's valuation has more than doubled.

🔴 **[10-19 18:40 Beijing] Nvidia reportedly requires Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron to use TSMC 3nm base die for custom HBM supply**  
Nvidia has requested Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, and Micron Technology to produce NVHBM (Nvidia's proprietary HBM technology) using TSMC's 3nm process for base die (Base Die), while core die (Core Die) uses 6th-gen DRAM technology. Samsung has reportedly accepted Nvidia's technical requirements. Samsung declined comment on customer-specific matters. Custom HBM's trend is shifting to modular base-die sourcing; memory makers still produce the core memory components. This reflects broader customization in the HBM supply chain rather than full outsourcing to foundries.

## Power & Datacenter Infrastructure (6)

🔴 **[10-19 22:00 Beijing] CNBC: The Race To Power AI Is Reshaping America's Electric Grid**  
AI data centers are driving unprecedented demand for electricity and putting renewed pressure on America's power grid to modernize its equipment and develop greener, more efficient sources of power. Google, Meta, Microsoft and Amazon are all spending millions of dollars on local infrastructure upgrades and companies like SpaceX are even building off-grid power plants to power their data centers.  
  
Google's planned 780-megawatt data center in Pine Island, Minnesota, could offer a model for powering the AI boom. In a proposed agreement with Xcel Energy, Google will support 1,900 megawatts of new wind, solar and battery capacity, while minimum payments and exit fees are intended to protect local ratepayers if demand falls short. The video examines whether such projects can make the grid cleaner without shifting costs to existing customers, why some energy experts argue that smaller data centers could make better use of existing infrastructure, and how utilities' financial incentives can complicate efforts to build less.  
_Video · YouTube · Google, Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, SpaceX, Xcel Energy · [Source](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Wh1zlJXKy1M)_

🔴 **[10-19 20:31 Beijing] AEP, Amazon and X-energy to jointly develop 960MW advanced nuclear power project in Indiana**  
American Electric Power (AEP) announced a joint development agreement with Amazon and advanced nuclear technology company X-energy to explore building a 960 megawatt nuclear power project in Indiana. Amazon plans to purchase the project's electricity through a long-term power purchase agreement, with contract revenue covering facility costs. The project will use advanced nuclear technology to meet growing electricity demand from data centers and other sectors.

**[10-19 20:38 Beijing] Cantor Fitzgerald maintains CoreWeave 'Buy' rating, sees capital payback period halved**  
Cantor Fitzgerald maintained CoreWeave's 'Buy' rating and $176 price target, arguing that recent significant stock price declines represent market overreaction, as AI compute demand remains strong with customers continuously seeking compute resources while market supply remains tight. The firm noted CoreWeave's recent contracts show significantly better economics than contracts from two years ago or even early this year, with capital expenditure payback period already shortened by nearly half, expected to improve company credit conditions and financing capability. Though CoreWeave's stock fell 23.5% to $61.39 over the past week and debt yield rose to 15%, CoreWeave announced a new partnership with AdaniConneX to plan 240 megawatts of additional data center capacity in Navi Mumbai, India. The company's revenue over the past 12 months grew 115% year-over-year.  
_News · Sina · CoreWeave · [Source](https://finance.sina.cn/7x24/2026-10-19/detail-inivumaf7712237.d.html)_
